target_customer: In-house legal teams and law firms negotiating contracts in Microsoft Word
problem: Lawyers redline contracts by hand against internal playbooks, which is slow and inconsistent; Pincites applied a company's playbook with large language models inside Word.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for a Word add-in
product_category: Legal AI contract redlining and negotiation

founders.name: Sona Sulakian
founders.background_notes: Former transactional attorney, patent attorney and legal tech strategy consultant per YC page.

founders.name: Mariam Sulakian
founders.background_notes: Product leader at GitHub and engineer at Meta.

founders.name: Grey Steil
founders.background_notes: Named in the YC launch post as a co-founder with a legal background; no bio found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A Word add-in applying playbooks with LLMs requires reliable clause detection and redline generation, plus Word integration, using 2023 language models for a legal audience that punishes errors.

defensibility.rationale: Customer playbooks and Word workflow create some stickiness, but well-funded legal AI vendors offered similar redlining.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Filevine acquired Pincites after a competitive process including bids from several legal AI firms, announced January 2026, and folded it into LOIS for Word.

market_need_then: Legal teams faced high volume contract review in Word; the GPT-4 wave in 2023 made automated first-pass review newly feasible. The founders had direct transactional law experience.

branding.domain_note: Used pincites.com, which now redirects (301) to a Filevine LOIS for Word page after the acquisition.

rebrands.why: Product folded into Filevine's LOIS platform after the acquisition.

brand_strength.rationale: The name plays on a legal term (pin cite) familiar to lawyers, but searches found no press about the brand itself and the name was retired after acquisition.

outcome_analysis: Pincites paired a lawyer-founder with an engineer from GitHub and Meta to build a Word-native redlining tool as large language models became usable, raised a $3M seed in September 2023 and sold to Filevine in a competitive process around December 2025. Filevine renamed the product LOIS for Word, so the brand ended while the team and technology continued. The price is undisclosed.
notes: The website pincites.com returned a 301 redirect to Filevine; the redirect target was not followed, so the live site text was not read. Funding conflicts: the YC page and VCBacked report a $3M seed in 2023 led by General Catalyst, while CB Insights reports $500K over 3 rounds including a convertible note. Round recorded from the YC page with VCBacked agreeing; lead investor named only by aggregators. Acquisition date varies (December 18 or 22, 2025; announced January 14, 2026). Dated competitor search returned only 2025 and 2026 comparison pages, so the list is empty.
